==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{multiple images
|direction = vertical
|image1 = Porcelain bowls, Ming dynasty, Hunan Museum.jpg
|caption1 = Ming dynasty porcelains ''(sense 4)''.
|image2 = Dresden Porcelain Collection - 07-1970.jpg
|caption2 = Dresden porcelains ''(sense 4)''.
}}

{{bor+|en|frm|porcelaine|t=cowrie, wampum; china, chinaware}}, from {{der|en|roa-oit|porcellana|t=cowrie; china, chinaware}}, from {{der|en|it|porcello||piglet}}. The material was so called because of its resemblance to the shell of the cowrie. Why the cowrie was named with a word meaning “piglet” is unclear.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɔːsəlɪn/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-porcelain.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɔɹs(ə)lɪn/|/ˈpɔɹs(ə)lən/|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpoːs(ɘ)lɘn/|a=NZ}}
* {{hyphenation|en|por|ce|lain}}, {{hyphenation|en|porc|lain|nocaption=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|usually|uncountable}} A [[hard]] [[white]] [[translucent]] [[ceramic]], [[originally]] [[made]] by firing [[kaolin]], [[quartz]], and [[feldspar]] at [[high]] [[temperature]]s but [[now]] [[also]] [[inclusive]] of [[similar]] [[artificial]] [[material]]s; [[also]] [[often]] {{lb|en|figurative}} [[such]] a [[material]] as a [[symbol]] of the [[fragility]], [[elegance]], etc. [[traditionally]] [[associated]] with porcelain [[goods]].
#: {{ux|en|[[tableware|Tableware]] and [[toilet]]s are both made of '''porcelain'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Andrew Martin|title=Underground Overground: A passenger's history of the Tube|publisher=Profile Books, {{ISBN|978-1846684777}}|page=136|text=Any power rail needs to be well insulated from earth, to minimise current leakage, and so the ''two'' power rails on the [[Underground]] sit on curiously genteel and antique-looking '''porcelain''' pots.}}
# {{lb|en|usually|uncountable}} {{syn of|en|china}}: porcelain [[tableware]].
#* {{c.|1530}}, letter in ''Original Letters Illustrative of English History'', Vol. II, p. 242:
#: {{ux|en|He [[set the table]] with our '''porcelain''' and stemware.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|obsolete}} {{syn of|en|kaolin}}: the [[kind of]] [[clay]] [[traditionally]] [[used]] in [[China]] to [[manufacture]] porcelain.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1599|translator=w:Richard Hakluyt|author=E. de Sande|title=The Principal Navigations, Voyages, Traffiques, and Discoveries of the English Nation|edition=2nd|volume=II|page=91
|passage=[...] that earthen or pliable matter commonly called '''porcellan''', which is pure white,... [[whereof|wherof]] vessels of all kinds are very curiously framed...}}
# {{lb|en|countable|now|_|usually|in the plural}} An [[object]] [[made]] of porcelain, {{lb|en|particularly}} [[art]] [[object]]s or [[item]]s of [[tableware]].
#: {{ux|en|The museum has an extensive collection of rare Chinese '''porcelains'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|rare}} {{syn of|en|cowrie}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1601|translator=Robert Johnson|author=Giovanni Botero|title=The Trauellers Breuiat, or, An Historicall Description of the Most Famous Kingdomes in the World|page=104
|passage=In the [[kingdoms|kingdomes]] of Caiacan and Carazan, [[certain]]e sea [[shells|shels]] are [[current|currant]], which some men [[term]]e '''Porcelline'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|obsolete|_|or|_|historic}} {{syn of|en|wampum}}: [[string]]s of [[shell]]s, [[bead]]s, etc. [[use]]d as [[ornamentation]] or [[currency]]; the [[composite]] [[shell]]s, [[bead]]s, etc.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1665|author=Pierre Esprit de Radisson|title=Voyages|edition=1885|page=49
|passage=We [[met]]t [[several]]l gangs of men to our greatest disadvantage, f[[for]] we [[were|weare]] forced to sing, and those that came to see us gave '''porcelaine''' to those that most did us injury.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|often|_|capitalized}} A [[kind of]] [[pigeon]] with [[deep]] [[brown]] and [[off-white]] [[feather]]s.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1855|journal=The Poultry Chronicle|issue=3|page=9
|passage=Those pretty spangled Toys [...] known by various names, as '''Porcelains''', Hyacinths, Ermines, &c.}}
# {{lb|en|programming|{{w|Git}}}} The set of {{w|Git}} commands, such as {{code|git commit}} or {{code|git checkout}}, which control the [[high-level#Adjective|high-level]] state of the [[repository#Noun|repository]], each typically combining the behaviour of multiple {{l|en|plumbing|id=Git}} commands.
#: {{coord|en|plumbing<id:Git>}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Jakub Narębski|chapter=Keeping History Clean|title=
Mastering Git|location=Birmingham, West Midlands|publisher=[[w:Packt|Packt Publishing Ltd.]]|year=2016|page=227|pageurl=https://books.google.ca/books?id=3vjJDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA227|passage=The {{code|git(1)}} manpage includes a list of all the Git commands separated into '''porcelain''' and plumbing. The distinction between plumbing and '''porcelain''' commands was mentioned as a tip in ''Chapter 4, Managing Your Worktree'', when we encountered the first low-level plumbing command without a user-facing and user-friendly '''porcelain''' equivalent.}}
